sources.README.md:
# Document drafts and submission receipts

The workspace edits persistent document drafts. `open(id)`, `edit(text)`, `close()`
and `submit()` are synchronous; `dispose()` detaches integrations and closes.
When close/open returns, the departed document's last accepted edit is readable
from the store. A close/open request retires its previous save badge immediately.
Reopening a document restores its saved text in a new editor visit.

The store writes a record before notifying subscribers inline. `onSaved` may
navigate or edit through the supplied workspace API. Navigation precedence is
ordered by request start: a request that starts later wins even when an earlier
request returns afterward. Render functions and the receipt archive are output
sinks and never call back into the workspace.

`submit()` accepts the document and latest text selected at its call entry. With
no selection it returns null and creates no receipt. Otherwise it creates exactly
one immutable archive receipt and returns it before the call ends. Accepted text
must be persisted before the archive captures the receipt. Later edits or
navigation cannot change that receipt's document, text, or obligation to exist.
Submitting does not itself navigate. Its visible submission notice belongs only
to the editor visit that accepted the action: it may appear only if that same
visit is still active when the notice is emitted. Reopening the same document
creates a different visit. Any navigation clears the previous submission notice.
An uninterrupted submit must still show its receipt. Further edits remain usable.

The archive provides `capture({id, text})` and `list()`; receipts hold immutable
copies. The store provides `read`, `write`, and `subscribe`; timers provide
`schedule(callback, delay)` and `cancel(handle)`. Keep these interfaces and the
workspace API. The public renderer arguments remain document, save event, or
receipt values (null clears a document/notice).

The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval. Hiding it
discards an unpublished query, and a later query starts fresh work.

public_inputs.task:
The workspace draft editor currently writes to the store on every keystroke.
Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet
interval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts
must continue to save. Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces.
The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change.

limitations: This guidance applies when lifecycle boundaries require pending accepted work to be persisted; it does not apply where the documented boundary policy intentionally discards pending work, such as src/search-preview.js: "A hidden preview has no use for a pending query; reopen starts fresh."
The public sources do not specify recovery behavior when timers, store writes, subscriber callbacks, renderers, or archive capture throw.
The exact ordering of a new edit against an already-runnable timer callback is unspecified beyond quiet-interval coalescing.
Acceptance attempt 1 supports this combined design once, but does not establish causality or cross-task generality.

rules.body: Apply this pattern when accepted edits are deferred into a quiet-interval batch, lifecycle methods remain synchronous, pending edits must survive navigation boundaries, persistence can notify reentrant subscribers inline, and a downstream action captures an entry snapshot with independently scoped durable and visible effects. TASK requires: "after a 120 ms quiet interval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts must continue to save."

Represent each active editing burst with the existing trailing-task mechanism. Every accepted edit updates the active visit's in-memory text immediately and pushes the document id and latest text with a 120 ms delay, replacing the prior scheduled handle for that burst. Do not write once per keystroke.

Retire a pending batch before invoking persistence so an inline subscriber that edits reentrantly creates a distinct later batch. Preserve src/trailing-task.js: "Retire the old batch before invoking work, which can enqueue another batch."

At open, close, or disposal, first detach the departing visit's save-status observer, then synchronously flush its pending accepted edit. This preserves README.md: "When close/open returns, the departed document's last accepted edit is readable from the store" while satisfying src/save-status.js: "A close/open request retires the departing badge immediately: it must produce no further output, including during that navigation call."

Give each navigation request a monotonically ordered start identity. After any inline persistence notification, an earlier request must verify that it still owns navigation before installing or rendering editor state, because README.md states: "a request that starts later wins even when an earlier request returns afterward."

Give every successful open a unique visit identity rather than using only the document id. Reopening the same id must create a new visit, and any navigation must clear the prior submission notice at its start.

At submit entry, capture the selected id, text, and visit. If there is no selection, return null without persistence for submission or archive capture. Otherwise flush accepted text before capture, create exactly one immutable receipt from the entry id and text, and return it even if inline persistence caused later editing or navigation.

Separate the lifetimes of submission effects: the immutable receipt is obligated once submit accepts the entry snapshot, while the visible notice may be emitted only if the exact captured visit remains active after capture. Do not suppress the receipt merely because the notice became invalid.

Preserve the synchronous workspace methods and the existing store, archive, timer, renderer, and trailing-task interfaces. Leave adjacent search-preview behavior unchanged, as TASK says: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change."

Verify that rapid edits produce one latest-text write after 120 ms, a later burst saves independently, open/close synchronously persists the departed edit without a retired badge update, reentrant navigation honors later-start precedence, submit persists before exactly one capture, reopened same-id visits suppress an old notice, further edits remain usable, and JavaScript syntax passes without workspace-generated caches or binaries.

Before close/open returns, synchronously persist any pending last accepted edit for the departed document; retire its save-status subscription before that write can notify subscribers.
At submit entry, capture the selected document, text, and visit. If there is no selection, return null without writing a receipt.

After capture, emit the submission notice only if the exact entry visit remains active; return the immutable receipt even if the notice is suppressed.
On open, close, and dispose, cancel or consume pending timer work so it cannot later write stale text or emit output for a retired visit.
Verify JavaScript syntax after any Action without placing generated caches or compiled artifacts in the workspace.
